claim: The immune system's ability to avoid autoimmune disease relies on tolerization of thymocytes to self-antigens whose expression and presentation by thymic medullary epithelial cells (mTECs) is controlled predominantly by Aire at the transcriptional level.
source: The ability of the immune system to avoid autoimmune disease relies on tolerization of thymocytes to self-antigens whose expression and presentation by thymic medullary epithelial cells (mTECs) is controlled predominantly by Aire at the transcriptional level and possibly regulated at other unrecognized levels.
evidence: This is established knowledge about immune tolerance and Aire function, supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Aire-sensitive gene expression is influenced by several molecular factors, some of which belong to the 3'end processing complex.
source: Aire-sensitive gene expression is influenced by several molecular factors, some of which belong to the 3'end processing complex, suggesting they might impact transcript stability and levels through an effect on 3'UTR shortening.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work (Abramson et al., 2010; Giraud et al., 2014) and data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Aire-sensitive genes display a pronounced preference for short-3'UTR transcript isoforms in mTECs.
source: We discovered that Aire-sensitive genes display a pronounced preference for short-3'UTR transcript isoforms in mTECs, a feature preceding Aire's expression and correlated with the preferential selection of proximal polyA sites by the 3'end processing complex.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data comparing d3'UTR ratios between Aire-sensitive and Aire-neutral genes shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The preference for short-3'UTR transcript isoforms in Aire-sensitive genes precedes Aire's expression.
source: We discovered that Aire-sensitive genes display a pronounced preference for short-3'UTR transcript isoforms in mTECs, a feature preceding Aire's expression and correlated with the preferential selection of proximal polyA sites by the 3'end processing complex.
evidence: This is supported by data from Aire-KO mTEChi showing similar d3'UTR ratio patterns (Figure 1E).

claim: The short-3'UTR preference of Aire-sensitive genes is correlated with the preferential selection of proximal polyA sites by the 3'end processing complex.
source: We discovered that Aire-sensitive genes display a pronounced preference for short-3'UTR transcript isoforms in mTECs, a feature preceding Aire's expression and correlated with the preferential selection of proximal polyA sites by the 3'end processing complex.
evidence: This is supported by PAR-CLIP data showing preferential CSTF2 binding at proximal pAs (Figure 2B).

claim: Clp1 promotes 3'UTR shortening associated with higher transcript stability and expression of Aire-sensitive genes.
source: Through an RNAi screen and generation of a lentigenic mouse, we found that one factor, Clp1, promotes 3'UTR shortening associated with higher transcript stability and expression of Aire-sensitive genes, revealing a post-transcriptional level of control of Aire-activated expression in mTECs.
evidence: This is supported by multiple experiments including shRNA knockdown in HEK293 cells (Figure 3) and lentigenic mouse data (Figure 4).

claim: Clp1-mediated regulation reveals a post-transcriptional level of control of Aire-activated expression in mTECs.
source: Through an RNAi screen and generation of a lentigenic mouse, we found that one factor, Clp1, promotes 3'UTR shortening associated with higher transcript stability and expression of Aire-sensitive genes, revealing a post-transcriptional level of control of Aire-activated expression in mTECs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing Clp1's effects on 3'UTR length and transcript stability.

claim: Central tolerance is shaped in the thymus and relies on a unique property of a subset of medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs).
source: Central tolerance is shaped in the thymus and relies on a unique property of a subset of medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs).
evidence: This is established knowledge in immunology, supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: mTEChi express high levels of MHC class II molecules and a huge diversity of self-antigens.
source: This subset is composed of mTEChi that express high levels of MHC class II molecules and a huge diversity of self-antigens (Danan-Gotthold et al., 2016; Kyewski and Klein, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Developing T lymphocytes in the thymus are exposed to a broad spectrum of self-antigens displayed by mTEChi.
source: Thus, developing T lymphocytes in the thymus are exposed to a broad spectrum of self-antigens displayed by mTEChi.
evidence: This is an inference based on the established knowledge about mTEChi function.

claim: Lymphocytes that recognize their cognate antigens undergo either negative selection or differentiate into thymic regulatory T cells.
source: Those lymphocytes that recognize their cognate antigens undergo either negative selection, thereby preventing the escape of potentially harmful autoreactive lymphocytes out of the thymus, or differentiate into thymic regulatory T cells beneficial for limiting autoreactivity (Cowan et al., 2013; Goodnow et al., 2005; Klein et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Self-antigens expressed by mTEChi include a large number of tissue-restricted antigens (TRAs).
source: Self-antigens expressed by mTEChi include a large number of tissue-restricted antigens (TRAs), so-named because they are normally restricted to one or a few peripheral tissues (Derbinski et al., 2001; Sansom et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: A large fraction of TRAs in mTEChi are induced by Aire.
source: A large fraction of these TRAs in mTEChi are induced by a single transcriptional activator that is expressed almost exclusively in these cells - the autoimmune regulator Aire.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Aire is expressed almost exclusively in mTEChi.
source: A large fraction of these TRAs in mTEChi are induced by a single transcriptional activator that is expressed almost exclusively in these cells - the autoimmune regulator Aire.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Mice deficient for the Aire gene exhibit impaired TRA expression in mTEChi.
source: Mice deficient for the Aire gene exhibit impaired TRA expression in mTEChi, whereas TRA expression remains normal in peripheral tissues of these mice.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Anderson et al., 2002.

claim: TRA expression remains normal in peripheral tissues of Aire-deficient mice.
source: Mice deficient for the Aire gene exhibit impaired TRA expression in mTEChi, whereas TRA expression remains normal in peripheral tissues of these mice.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Anderson et al., 2002.

claim: Aire knockout mice develop autoantibodies directed at some TRAs.
source: Consistent with inadequate development of central tolerance, Aire knockout (KO) mice develop autoantibodies directed at some of these TRAs, resulting in immune infiltrates in multiple tissues (Anderson et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Anderson et al., 2002.

claim: Aire knockout mice develop immune infiltrates in multiple tissues.
source: Consistent with inadequate development of central tolerance, Aire knockout (KO) mice develop autoantibodies directed at some of these TRAs, resulting in immune infiltrates in multiple tissues (Anderson et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Anderson et al., 2002.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in the human AIRE gene result in autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1.
source: Correspondingly, loss-of-function mutations in the human AIRE gene result in a multi-organ autoimmune disorder known as autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1 (Nagamine et al., 1997; Peterson et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Nagamine et al., 1997 and Peterson et al., 2004.

claim: Several molecular factors have been identified that activate the expression of prototypic Aire-sensitive genes in cell lines expressing Aire ectopically.
source: Significant progress has been made, notably through the identification of a number of molecular factors that further activate the expression of prototypic Aire-sensitive genes in a model employing cell lines that express Aire ectopically by transfection with a constitutive Aire expression vector (Abramson et al., 2010; Giraud et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Abramson et al., 2010 and Giraud et al., 2014.

claim: The PRKDC-PARP1-SUPT16H complex plays a role in relaxation of chromatin in front of the elongating RNA polymerase II.
source: These studies revealed a role for relaxation of chromatin in front of the elongating RNA polymerase (RNAP) II by the PRKDC-PARP1-SUPT16H complex (Abramson et al., 2010) and for an HNRNPL-associated release of the stalled RNAPII (Giraud et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Abramson et al., 2010.

claim: HNRNPL is associated with release of stalled RNAPII.
source: These studies revealed a role for relaxation of chromatin in front of the elongating RNA polymerase (RNAP) II by the PRKDC-PARP1-SUPT16H complex (Abramson et al., 2010) and for an HNRNPL-associated release of the stalled RNAPII (Giraud et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Giraud et al., 2014.

claim: Seven identified factors (CLP1, DDX5, DDX17, PABPC1, PRKDC, SUPT16H and PARP1) have been reported to belong to the 3' end processing complex.
source: Among the identified factors, seven of them, namely CLP1, DDX5, DDX17, PABPC1, PRKDC, SUPT16H and PARP1, have been reported to belong to the large multi-subunit 3' end processing complex (de Vries et al., 2000; Shi et al., 2009) which controls pre-mRNA cleavage and polyadenylation at polyA sites (pAs) (Colgan and Manley, 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to de Vries et al., 2000 and Shi et al., 2009.

claim: The 3' end processing complex controls pre-mRNA cleavage and polyadenylation at polyA sites.
source: Among the identified factors, seven of them, namely CLP1, DDX5, DDX17, PABPC1, PRKDC, SUPT16H and PARP1, have been reported to belong to the large multi-subunit 3' end processing complex (de Vries et al., 2000; Shi et al., 2009) which controls pre-mRNA cleavage and polyadenylation at polyA sites (pAs) (Colgan and Manley, 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Colgan and Manley, 1997.

claim: 70-79% of protein-coding genes in mammal genomes have multiple polyA sites mostly located in 3'UTRs.
source: Deep sequencing approaches have revealed that the vast majority of protein-coding genes in mammal genomes (70–79%) have multiple pAs mostly located in 3'UTRs (Derti et al., 2012; Hoque et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Derti et al., 2012 and Hoque et al., 2013.

claim: The 3' end processing complex is composed of a core effector sub-complex comprising CLP1 and a number of accessory proteins.
source: The 3' end processing complex is composed of a core effector sub-complex comprising CLP1 (de Vries et al., 2000; Mandel et al., 2008) and a number of accessory proteins that include DDX5, DDX17, PABPC1, PRKDC, SUPT16H and PARP1 (Shi et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to de Vries et al., 2000; Mandel et al., 2008; and Shi et al., 2009.

claim: Clp1 has been reported to favor proximal pA selection in yeast based on depletion experiments.
source: Although the individual roles of accessory proteins on differential pA usage remain largely unknown, the core protein Clp1 has been reported to favor proximal pA selection in yeast based on depletion experiments (Holbein et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Holbein et al., 2011.

claim: Increasing levels of Clp1 bound to the 3' end processing complex favor proximal pA selection and shorter 3'UTR isoforms.
source: Similarly, increasing levels of Clp1 bound to the 3' end processing complex was also shown to favor proximal pA selection and shorter 3'UTR isoforms (Johnson et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Johnson et al., 2011.

claim: A preference for distal pA selection was reported for higher Clp1 levels in a mouse myoblast cell line based on siRNA Clp1 loss-of-function experiments.
source: In contrast, a preference for distal pA selection was reported for higher Clp1 levels in a mouse myoblast cell line based on siRNA Clp1 loss-of-function experiments (Li et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Li et al., 2015.

claim: Aire-sensitive genes show a significant shift towards smaller d3'UTR ratios compared to Aire-neutral genes in WT mTEChi.
source: We found a significant shift towards smaller ratios, revealing a preference of Aire-sensitive genes for short-3'UTR isoforms in mTEChi (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 1—source data 3 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1C with statistical significance P=1.5×10^-15.

claim: The preference of Aire-sensitive genes for smaller d3'UTR ratios in mTEChi is independent of the levels of gene expression.
source: While the d3'UTR ratios vary dramatically across genes, at all expression levels, the loess-fitted curve of the Aire-sensitive genes is significantly lower than the one of the Aire-neutral genes, therefore revealing a preference of Aire-sensitive genes for smaller d3'UTR ratios in mTEChi that is independent of the levels of gene expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A comparing d3'UTR ratios across expression levels.

claim: The short-3'UTR isoform preference is observed preferentially in Aire-sensitive genes regardless of whether or not they are TRA genes.
source: In these mTEChi, the short-3'UTR isoform preference was observed preferentially in Aire-sensitive genes regardless of whether or not they were TRA genes (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1D comparing TRA and non-TRA genes.

claim: The preference for short-3'UTR isoforms of Aire-sensitive genes is preserved in Aire-KO mTEChi.
source: We observed a preference for the smaller ratios (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and Figure 1—source data 3 and 4) in Aire-sensitive versus neutral genes in the Aire-KO cells.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data from Aire-KO mTEChi shown in Figure 1E with statistical significance P=1.9×10^-14.

claim: The preference of Aire-sensitive genes for smaller d3'UTR ratios in Aire-KO mTEChi is independent of the levels of gene expression.
source: For these KO mTEChi, we once again examined the d3'UTR ratios across all expression levels of both Aire-sensitive and neutral genes and again, like in WT mTEChi, found that the preference of Aire-sensitive genes for smaller d3'UTR ratios was independent of the levels of gene expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Approximately 90% of Aire-sensitive genes that exhibited small d3'UTR ratios (<0.25) in WT mTEChi also showed small d3'UTR ratios in Aire-KO mTEChi.
source: We further noted that the majority (~90%) of Aire-sensitive genes that exhibited small d3'UTR ratios (<0.25) in WT mTEChi were also characterized by small d3'UTR ratios in Aire-KO mTEChi (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The short-3'UTR isoform preference of Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi is specific to those genes responsive to Aire, whether or not Aire is actually present.
source: Together, these observations showed that the short-3'UTR isoform preference of Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi was specific to those genes responsive to Aire, whether or not Aire was actually present.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing similar d3'UTR patterns in WT and Aire-KO mTEChi.

claim: Aire-sensitive TRA genes exhibit an increased proportion of short-3'UTR transcript isoforms in mTEChi versus a majority of peripheral tissues.
source: Taking the Aire-sensitive TRA genes individually, we compared their d3'UTR ratios in mTEChi versus their respective tissue of expression and found a dramatic bias towards higher ratios in peripheral tissues, confirming the preference of Aire-sensitive TRA genes for short-3'UTR transcript isoforms in mTEChi, as compared to the periphery (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1H comparing d3'UTR ratios between mTEChi and peripheral tissues.

claim: Small d3'UTR ratios of Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi are not correlated with the sequencing depth of the mTEChi RNA-seq libraries.
source: In addition, we confirmed that small d3'UTR ratios of Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi were not correlated with the sequencing depth of the mTEChi RNA-seq libraries nor with the length of the generated reads (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Small d3'UTR ratios of Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi are not correlated with the length of the generated reads.
source: In addition, we confirmed that small d3'UTR ratios of Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi were not correlated with the sequencing depth of the mTEChi RNA-seq libraries nor with the length of the generated reads (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: HEK293 cells are negative for AIRE expression.
source: To circumvent this issue, we used the HEK293 cell line for these experiments. HEK293 cells are (i) negative for AIRE expression, (ii) responsive to the transactivation activity of transfected Aire (Abramson et al., 2010; Giraud et al., 2012), and (iii) have been profiled for the RNA binding of the 3' end processing components by Martin et al. by PAR-CLIP experiments (Martin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about HEK293 cells.

claim: HEK293 cells are responsive to the transactivation activity of transfected Aire.
source: To circumvent this issue, we used the HEK293 cell line for these experiments. HEK293 cells are (i) negative for AIRE expression, (ii) responsive to the transactivation activity of transfected Aire (Abramson et al., 2010; Giraud et al., 2012), and (iii) have been profiled for the RNA binding of the 3' end processing components by Martin et al. by PAR-CLIP experiments (Martin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Abramson et al., 2010 and Giraud et al., 2012.

claim: HEK293 cells have been profiled for the RNA binding of the 3' end processing components by PAR-CLIP experiments.
source: To circumvent this issue, we used the HEK293 cell line for these experiments. HEK293 cells are (i) negative for AIRE expression, (ii) responsive to the transactivation activity of transfected Aire (Abramson et al., 2010; Giraud et al., 2012), and (iii) have been profiled for the RNA binding of the 3' end processing components by Martin et al. by PAR-CLIP experiments (Martin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Martin et al., 2012.

claim: Aire-sensitive genes show significantly lower d3'UTR ratios compared to Aire-neutral genes in both Aire-transfected and Ctr-transfected HEK293 cells.
source: Similarly to what we found in WT and Aire-KO mTEChi, we observed in Aire-transfected and Ctr-transfected HEK293 cells significant lower d3'UTR ratios for genes identified by Aire transfection to be Aire-sensitive versus Aire-neutral genes (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2A with statistical significance P=1.2×10^-13 for Ctr-transfected and P=1.4×10^-12 for Aire-transfected HEK293 cells.

claim: Lower d3'UTR ratios correlate with the preferential location of the 3' end processing complex at proximal pAs for Aire-neutral genes.
source: We first validated for Aire-neutral genes that lower d3'UTR ratios correlated with the preferential location of the 3' end processing complex at proximal pAs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by PAR-CLIP data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The 3' end processing complex shows a dramatic preference for proximal pAs versus distal pAs at Aire-sensitive genes in HEK293 cells.
source: Then we compared the location of the complex between the Aire-sensitive and neutral genes, and found a dramatic preference for proximal pAs versus distal pAs at Aire-sensitive genes (Figure 2B), showing that the 3' end processing complex was already in place at proximal pAs of Aire-sensitive genes before Aire expression was enforced in HEK293 cells.
evidence: This is supported by PAR-CLIP data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The 3' end processing complex is already in place at proximal pAs of Aire-sensitive genes before Aire expression in HEK293 cells.
source: Then we compared the location of the complex between the Aire-sensitive and neutral genes, and found a dramatic preference for proximal pAs versus distal pAs at Aire-sensitive genes (Figure 2B), showing that the 3' end processing complex was already in place at proximal pAs of Aire-sensitive genes before Aire expression was enforced in HEK293 cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the PAR-CLIP data in AIRE-negative HEK293 cells.

claim: CLP1, DDX5, DDX17, PARP1 and HNRNPL contribute to 3'UTR shortening in HEK293 cells.
source: With a threshold of at least two shRNAs per gene producing a significant excess of genes with increased d3'UTR ratios, we found that CLP1, DDX5, DDX17, PARP1 and HNRNPL contributed to 3'UTR shortening in HEK293 cells (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments and microarray data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Knockdown of CPSF6 reveals a skewed distribution towards decreased d3'UTR ratios.
source: As a control, we also performed knockdown of CPSF6, a core member of the 3' end processing complex, that has been consistently reported to promote general 3'UTR lengthening (Li et al., 2015; Martin et al., 2012). As expected, knockdown of CPSF6 revealed a skewed distribution towards decreased d3'UTR ratios (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and citations to Li et al., 2015 and Martin et al., 2012.

claim: CLP1 is the only factor among the tested candidates whose knockdown by two distinct shRNAs led to a significant reduction of the expression of Aire-sensitive genes with proximal pAs.
source: For each candidate factor, we computed the rank of differential expression of all genes in Ctr versus HEK293 cells knockdown for the tested candidate, and found that CLP1 was the only gene whose knockdown by two distinct shRNAs led to a significant reduction of the expression of Aire-sensitive genes (Figure 3B), focusing our subsequent study on CLP1.
evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The effect of CLP1 on Aire-sensitive gene expression in HEK293 cells is dependent on the potential of Aire-sensitive genes to switch from using a distal to a proximal pA site.
source: Our findings regarding the differential response of pA+ and pA- genes to CLP1 loss-of-function suggested that the effect of CLP1 on Aire-sensitive gene expression in HEK293 cells was dependent on the potential of Aire-sensitive genes to switch from using a distal to a proximal pA site.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the differential effects on pA+ versus pA- genes shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: CLP1 knockdown results in a statistically significant increase of the median d3'UTR ratios of Aire-sensitive genes in HEK293 cells.
source: Comparison of the 3' end profiles revealed a statistically significant increase of the median d3'UTR ratios of Aire-sensitive genes for both CLP1 hit shRNAs (Figure 3D, Left), showing that CLP1 is able to promote 3'UTR shortening at Aire-sensitive genes in HEK293 cells.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3D with statistical significance p<0.05.

claim: The effect of CLP1 on 3'UTR shortening preferentially affects the Aire-sensitive genes in HEK293 cells.
source: In contrast to Aire-sensitive genes, only small, statistically insignificant increases of d3'UTR ratios of Aire-neutral genes could be detected in CLP1 knockdown HEK293 cells, indicating that the effect of CLP1 on 3'UTR shortening preferentially affects the Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3D comparing Aire-sensitive and Aire-neutral genes.

claim: An enhanced proportion of genes subject to CLP1-mediated 3'UTR shortening is observed among the Aire-sensitive versus neutral genes in HEK293 cells.
source: The preferential 3'UTR shortening effect of CLP1 at Aire-sensitive genes was further supported by the observation of an enhanced proportion of genes subject to CLP1-mediated 3'UTR shortening among the Aire-sensitive versus neutral genes in HEK293 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: CLP1 knockdown results in selective reduction of the expression of Aire-sensitive genes that have alternative proximal pAs in HEK293 cells.
source: Finally, using RNA-seq data, we confirmed the effect of CLP1 knockdown on the selective reduction of the expression of Aire-sensitive genes that were annotated to have alternative proximal pAs in HEK293 cells (Figure 3D, Right).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3D with statistical significance p<0.05.

claim: The extent of the effect of CLP1 knockdown on the levels of Aire-sensitive gene expression in Aire-transfected HEK293 cells is similar to, although slightly stronger than, the effect in AIRE-negative HEK293 cells.
source: Furthermore, we observed that the extent of the effect of CLP1 knockdown on the levels of Aire-sensitive gene expression in Aire-transfected HEK293 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 4) was similar, although slightly stronger than the one we described above in AIRE-negative HEK293 cells.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: CLP1 promotes 3'UTR shortening and increases expression of Aire-sensitive genes with proximal pAs.
source: Together these findings showed that CLP1 is able to promote 3'UTR shortening and increase expression of Aire-sensitive genes with proximal pAs, supporting a linked mechanism between CLP1-promoted 3'UTR shortening and gene expression enhancement at Aire-sensitive genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the HEK293 knockdown experiments.

claim: A lentigenic Clp1 knockdown mouse was generated with 60% reduction of Clp1 mRNA levels in GFP+ mTEChi.
source: Of the 19 pups that we obtained with integration of both plasmids, two pups were expressing, after doxycycline treatment, the multi-miR in mTEChi and one pup was exhibiting a 60% reduction of Clp1 mRNA levels in GFP+ (Clp1 knockdown) versus GFP- (Ctr) mTEChi taken from the same mouse.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental generation of the lentigenic mouse.

claim: Clp1 knockdown results in a significant increase of d3'UTR ratios of Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi.
source: We found a significant increase of d3'UTR ratios of Aire-sensitive genes following Clp1 knockdown in mTEChi, as well as a less pronounced effect that does not reach significance for Aire-neutral genes regardless of whether they are TRA genes or not.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data from lentigenic mice shown in Figure 4B with p=0.044.

claim: The effect of Clp1 on 3'UTR shortening preferentially affects Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi.
source: This finding therefore supports that the effect of Clp1 on 3'UTR shortening preferentially affects Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi (Figure 4B and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data from lentigenic mice shown in Figure 4B.

claim: An enhanced proportion of genes subject to Clp1-mediated 3'UTR shortening is observed among the Aire-sensitive versus neutral genes in mTEChi.
source: The preferential 3'UTR shortening effect of Clp1 at Aire-sensitive genes was further supported by the observation of an enhanced proportion of genes subject to Clp1-mediated 3'UTR shortening among the Aire-sensitive versus neutral genes in mTEChi (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2 with statistical significance P=8.9×10^-15.

claim: Clp1 knockdown results in a significant reduction of expression of Aire-sensitive genes with potential proximal pAs in mTEChi.
source: We then compared the levels of expression of the Aire-sensitive genes with potential proximal pAs in Ctr versus Clp1 knockdown mTEChi and found, in contrast to Aire-neutral genes, a significant reduction following Clp1 knockdown (Figure 4C, Left).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4C with statistical significance P=1.6×10^-9.

claim: Aire-sensitive genes that undergo a higher than 2-fold d3'UTR ratio decrease in Ctr versus Clp1 knockdown lentigenic mTEChi exhibit higher expression values.
source: The link between Clp1-mediated 3'UTR shortening and increased expression at Aire-sensitive genes is strengthened by the observation that the Aire-sensitive genes that undergo a higher than 2-fold d3'UTR ratio decrease in Ctr versus Clp1 knockdown lentigenic mTEChi, exhibit higher expression values (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: The effect of Clp1 knockdown is dampened for the Aire-sensitive genes lacking potential proximal pAs.
source: As observed in HEK293 cells, the effect of Clp1 knockdown was dampened for the Aire-sensitive genes lacking potential proximal pAs (Figure 4C, Right).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The expression of genes without proximal pAs is globally reduced in comparison to genes with proximal pAs.
source: We also found that the expression of the genes without proximal pAs was globally reduced in comparison to the genes with proximal pAs, supporting a linked mechanism between proximal pA usage and increased gene expression in mTEChi.
evidence: This is an observation from the RNA-seq data supporting the link between pA usage and expression.

claim: Clp1 promotes 3'UTR shortening of the transcripts upregulated by Aire in mTEChi and enhances their level of expression through proximal pA usage.
source: Altogether these results showed that Clp1 promotes 3'UTR shortening of the transcripts upregulated by Aire in mTEChi and strongly suggested that it enhances their level of expression through proximal pA usage.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lentigenic mouse experiments.

claim: Clp1 shows higher expression in mTEChi in comparison to a wide variety of tissues.
source: A role for Clp1 in mTEChi was further supported by its higher expression in mTEChi in comparison to a wide variety of tissues for which we collected RNA-seq datasets (Shen et al., 2012; van den Berghe et al., 2013; Warren et al., 2013; Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4D with statistical significance P=2×10^-4.

claim: None of the other candidate factors (Hnrnpl, Ddx5, Ddx17 and Parp1) that contributed to 3'UTR shortening in HEK293 cells were over-represented in mTEChi.
source: As a comparison, none of the other candidate factors, Hnrnpl, Ddx5, Ddx17 and Paprp1 that contributed to 3'UTR shortening in HEK293 cells, were over-represented in mTEChi (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: Higher expression of Clp1 at the protein level in mTEChi versus their precursor cells (mTEClo), cells from the whole thymus, and the predominant thymus CD45+ leukocyte fraction was validated.
source: Importantly, we also validated higher expression of Clp1 at the protein level in mTEChi versus their precursor cells, mTEClo (Gäbler et al., 2007; Hamazaki et al., 2007), cells from the whole thymus, and also the predominant thymus CD45+ leukocyte fraction (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: Clp1 expression levels are similar in WT and Aire-KO mTEChi.
source: In addition, a role for Clp1 independent of Aire's action on genes expression was supported by the observed similar levels of Clp1 expression in WT and Aire-KO mTEChi (Figure 4—figure supplement 6A) and the lack of evidence for Aire and CLP1 interaction (Figure 4—figure supplement 6B).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 6A.

claim: There is a lack of evidence for Aire and CLP1 interaction.
source: In addition, a role for Clp1 independent of Aire's action on genes expression was supported by the observed similar levels of Clp1 expression in WT and Aire-KO mTEChi (Figure 4—figure supplement 6A) and the lack of evidence for Aire and CLP1 interaction (Figure 4—figure supplement 6B).
evidence: This is supported by coimmunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 6B.

claim: There is a significant correlation between higher Clp1 expression and lower d3'UTR ratios across peripheral tissues for the Aire-sensitive TRA genes.
source: Finally, we found a significant correlation between higher Clp1 expression and lower d3'UTR ratios across peripheral tissues for the Aire-sensitive TRA genes (Figure 4E, Top).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4E with p=0.002.

claim: No significant correlation is observed between Clp1 expression and d3'UTR ratios for Aire-neutral genes across peripheral tissues.
source: In contrast, no such significant correlation was observed for Aire-neutral genes (Figure 4E, Bottom).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The effect of Clp1 on 3'UTR shortening at Aire-sensitive genes is independent of Aire's action on gene expression, general across cell types, and conserved upon upregulation of gene expression by Aire in mTEChi.
source: These findings indicate that the effect of Clp1 on 3'UTR shortening at Aire-sensitive genes is independent of Aire's action on gene expression, general across cell types, and conserved upon upregulation of gene expression by Aire in mTEChi.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of evidence including expression data and correlation analysis.

claim: Aire-sensitive genes subject to Clp1-driven 3'UTR shortening show increasing preservation of transcript levels at 3, 6, and 12 hours after transcription inhibition, indicating transcript stabilization.
source: Comparison of the two gene sets in ActD-treated versus control samples revealed that the Aire-sensitive genes subject to Clp1-driven 3'UTR shortening were initially comparable in their changes in transcript levels upon transcription inhibition to the changes for Aire-sensitive genes that showed no 3'UTR shortening but then showed increasing preservation of transcript levels at 3 hr and 6 or 12 hr, indicating a stabilization of this subset of 3'UTR-shortened transcripts (Figure 5; p=2.1×10−4, 1.3 × 10−12, and 5.6 × 10−10 at 3, 6 and 12 hr, respectively).
evidence: This is supported by ActD treatment experiments shown in Figure 5 with statistical significance at multiple timepoints.

claim: The Clp1-promoted 3'UTR shortening at Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi is associated with higher transcript stability.
source: Therefore, the Clp1-promoted 3'UTR shortening at Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi is indeed associated with higher transcript stability.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ActD treatment experiments.

claim: 346 miRNA-specific target gene sets have significantly reduced expression in mTEChi versus mTEClo.
source: We found 346 miRNA-specific target gene sets that had significantly reduced expression in mTEChi versus mTEClo (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis comparing mTEChi and mTEClo.

claim: No miRNA-specific target gene sets had reduced expression in mTEClo versus mTEChi.
source: In sharp contrast, we did not detect any of the miRNA-specific target gene sets that had reduced expression in mTEClo versus mTEChi.
evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis comparing mTEChi and mTEClo.

claim: miRNAs are an important contributor to transcript destabilization in mTEChi.
source: This suggests that miRNAs are an important contributor to transcript destabilization in mTEChi and that this effect is similar or less for the same miRNA target sets in mTEClo cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the GSEA analysis showing reduced expression of miRNA target gene sets in mTEChi.

claim: 46% of Aire-sensitive genes subject to Clp1-promoted shortening have one or more conserved miRNA target sites in the d3'UTR of their longer-transcript isoforms.
source: We found a large proportion of these cases (46%) had one or more such conserved miRNA target sites, providing a specific miRNA de-repression mechanism due to 3'UTR shortening for a large fraction of the Aire-sensitive genes.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of TargetScan database predictions.

claim: Clp1 promotes 3'UTR shortening of the transcripts upregulated by Aire in mTEChi, and these transcripts are associated with enhanced stability.
source: In our present study, we demonstrated that Clp1 promotes 3'UTR shortening of the transcripts upregulated by Aire in mTEChi, and that these transcripts are associated with an enhanced stability, revealing a post-transcriptional mechanism whose escape leads to higher levels of expression of Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple experiments.

claim: Clp1-driven 3'UTR shortening reveals a post-transcriptional mechanism that leads to higher levels of expression of Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi.
source: In our present study, we demonstrated that Clp1 promotes 3'UTR shortening of the transcripts upregulated by Aire in mTEChi, and that these transcripts are associated with an enhanced stability, revealing a post-transcriptional mechanism whose escape leads to higher levels of expression of Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: The effect of Clp1 on Aire-sensitive genes is not restricted to mTEChi nor dependent on Aire's action.
source: We found that this 3'UTR shortening was driven by Clp1 in mTEChi but also in Aire-non-expressing HEK293 cells, in which the level of Aire-sensitive gene expression is weak but still detectable by RNA-seq, thus showing that the effect of Clp1 on Aire-sensitive genes was not restricted to mTEChi nor dependent on Aire's action.
evidence: This is supported by experiments in both mTEChi and HEK293 cells.

claim: Clp1 is a ubiquitous protein showing higher expression in mTEChi than in mTEClo, CD45+ thymic cells or thymic cells taken as a whole.
source: Clp1 is a ubiquitous protein showing higher expression in mTEChi than in mTEClo, CD45+ thymic cells or thymic cells taken as a whole, but also showing higher gene expression in comparison with a large range of peripheral tissue cells.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq and flow cytometry data.

claim: The level of Clp1 expression is significantly high in 14.5 embryonic liver cells.
source: Interestingly, we found that the level of Clp1 expression was also significantly high in 14.5 embryonic liver cells, cells that have been reported to undergo sustained cellular activation leading to proliferation and maturation into hepatocytes (Kung et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data and citation to Kung et al., 2010.

claim: Higher levels of Clp1 expression are correlated with higher proportions of short-3'UTR transcript isoforms of tissue-restricted Aire-sensitive genes across peripheral tissues.
source: Notably, we showed that higher levels of Clp1 expression were correlated with higher proportions of short-3'UTR transcript isoforms of tissue-restricted Aire-sensitive genes across peripheral tissues, suggesting the existence of a Clp1-promoted 3'UTR shortening mechanism occurring in a variety of cell types and, among those cell types we surveyed, most pronounced in mTEChi.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis across multiple tissues.

claim: The Clp1-driven 3'UTR shortening mechanism is already in place in mTEChi before Aire is activated.
source: The observation that the levels of Clp1 expression and the distributions of the short-3'UTR transcript isoforms of Aire-sensitive genes were similar between Aire-KO and WT mTEChi, strongly suggests that the Clp1-driven 3'UTR shortening mechanism is already in place in mTEChi before Aire is activated.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison of WT and Aire-KO mTEChi data.

claim: The independence of Aire's action on gene expression and the effect of Clp1 on 3'UTR shortening is consistent with the lack of direct interaction between Aire and Clp1.
source: The independence of Aire's action on gene expression and the effect of Clp1 on 3'UTR shortening is also consistent with the lack of direct interaction found between Aire and Clp1.
evidence: This is supported by coimmunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: Sensitivity to Aire and Clp1 effects have a higher-rate of co-occurrence in the same set of genes.
source: Although these effects of Aire and Clp1 appear decoupled, it is also apparent as noted that sensitivity to these Aire and Clp1 effects have a higher-rate of co-occurrence in the same set of genes.
evidence: This is an observation from the data showing overlap between Aire-sensitive and Clp1-responsive genes.

claim: Clp1 is a member of the core 3' end processing complex that is preferentially located at proximal pAs of Aire-sensitive genes in HEK293 cells.
source: Clp1 is a member of the core 3' end processing complex that we showed to be preferentially located at proximal pAs of Aire-sensitive genes in HEK293 cells, indicating that the effect of Clp1 on 3'UTR shortening could result from enhanced recruitment of the 3' end processing complex to proximal pAs.
evidence: This is supported by PAR-CLIP data showing CSTF2 binding patterns.

claim: The effect of Clp1 on 3'UTR shortening could result from enhanced recruitment of the 3' end processing complex to proximal pAs.
source: Clp1 is a member of the core 3' end processing complex that we showed to be preferentially located at proximal pAs of Aire-sensitive genes in HEK293 cells, indicating that the effect of Clp1 on 3'UTR shortening could result from enhanced recruitment of the 3' end processing complex to proximal pAs.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed binding patterns.

claim: Similar modes of action involving members of the core 3' end processing complex have been described for Clp1 in yeast and Cpsf6 in humans.
source: Similar modes of action, involving members of the core 3' end processing complex and resulting in transcripts with either shorter or longer 3'UTRs have been described for Clp1 in yeast (Johnson et al., 2011) and Cpsf6 in humans (Gruber et al., 2012; Martin et al., 2012), respectively.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Johnson et al., 2011; Gruber et al., 2012; and Martin et al., 2012.

claim: 3'UTRs are potent sensors of post-transcriptional repression mediated by miRNAs, resulting in mRNA destabilization and degradation.
source: 3'UTRs have been described as potent sensors of the post-transcriptional repression mediated by miRNAs, resulting in mRNA destabilization and degradation (Bartel, 2009; Jonas and Izaurralde, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Bartel, 2009 and Jonas and Izaurralde, 2015.

claim: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) contribute to the regulation of transcript stability depending on the type of cis regulatory elements they recognize on 3'UTRs.
source: In addition to miRNAs, RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) also contribute the regulation of transcript stability depending on the type of cis regulatory elements that they recognize on 3'UTRs, triggering either repression or activation signals (Spies et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Spies et al., 2013.

claim: The finding that transcripts controlled by Aire and subjected to Clp1-promoted 3'UTR shortening escape miRNA-mediated post-transcriptional repression is consistent with reports showing maturation-dependent expression of miRNAs correlates with Aire expression in mTEChi.
source: The finding that the transcripts controlled by Aire and subjected to Clp1-promoted 3'UTR shortening in mTEChi escape the miRNA-mediated post-transcriptional repression that proves to be stronger in mTEChi than in mTEClo, is consistent with recent reports showing that maturation-dependent expression of miRNAs correlates with the expression of Aire in mTEChi (Ucar et al., 2013) and that Aire is able to control the expression of miRNAs in a murine mTEC line (Macedo et al., 2015) or in mTEChi in vivo through the comparison of WT and Aire null mutant thymi (Ucar et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ucar et al., 2013 and Macedo et al., 2015.

claim: Some classical Aire-dependent TRAs exhibit profound refractoriness in reconstructed networking interactions with miRNAs, in contrast to Aire-independent TRA transcripts.
source: Interestingly, it has also been reported that, in contrast to Aire-independent TRA transcripts, some classical Aire-dependent TRAs exhibit profound refractoriness in reconstructed networking interactions with miRNAs (Macedo et al., 2015; Oliveira et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Macedo et al., 2015 and Oliveira et al., 2016.

claim: An alteration in 3'UTRs of Aire-dependent TRA transcripts has been proposed to explain the refractoriness to miRNA interactions.
source: An alteration in 3'UTRs of Aire-dependent TRA transcripts has been proposed to explain this observation (Passos et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Passos et al., 2015.

claim: The study provides evidence that Aire-sensitive genes undergo 3'UTR shortening resulting in the escape of the generated shortened transcripts from the miRNA-mediated post-transcriptional repression in mTEChi.
source: Consistent with this proposal, our study provides evidence that Aire-sensitive genes undergo 3'UTR shortening resulting in the escape of the generated shortened transcripts from the miRNA-mediated post-transcriptional repression in mTEChi.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Short 3'UTRs have been shown to shift the surface localization of membrane proteins and the functional cell compartment of other types of proteins, in favor of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER).
source: In addition to impacting transcript stability through the escape of the post-transcriptional repression, short 3'UTRs have also been shown to shift the surface localization of membrane proteins and the functional cell compartment of other types of proteins, in favor of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) (Berkovits and Mayr, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Berkovits and Mayr, 2015.

claim: Clp1-driven 3'UTR shortening at Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi might favor routing of Aire-dependent self-antigens to the ER, potentially enhancing their presentation to self-reactive T lymphocytes.
source: Thus, one interesting hypothesis for future study is that Clp1-driven 3'UTR shortening at Aire-sensitive genes in mTEChi might not only impact the expression of Aire-dependent self-antigens but also favor their routing to the ER, from where they will be processed and presented, potentially enhancing their presentation to self-reactive T lymphocytes and, subsequently, central tolerance and protection against autoimmune manifestations.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential future implications of the findings.
